STEP 1 - Vessel type: shallow-to-medium bowl. The food sits in a white bowl with a curved inner wall visible on the left and a rounded rim; the food surface is roughly at rim level, so it is a shallow bowl or wide salad bowl.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: this looks like a salad or serving bowl, about 20-25 cm.
b) Reference cue: broccoli florets are about 4 cm. Across the bowl I count roughly 5-6 floret widths, so width ≈ 22-24 cm.
Reconciled width: about 22 cm.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Spinach/leafy greens (raw, base layer covering much of the bowl): the bowl interior is about 22 cm wide. Greens cover most of the surface, roughly 75% of area: 0.75 x 380 cm² ≈ 285 cm². Loose leaves 2 cm thick on average gives ~570 ml x 0.15 = ~85 g.
- Broccoli florets (cooked/steamed, chopped): about 6 visible florets, each ~15 g, plus hidden ones, total ~ 120 g. Counting as chopped vegetable, ~100 g.
- Kalamata-type olives or dark berries: about 12 visible, plus ~6 hidden = 18 x 4 g = ~72 g.
- Shaved Parmesan cheese: a generous layer over the centre, ~30 g.
- Avocado slices (pale green pieces): ~40 g.
- Dressing (light oil/vinaigrette, visible sheen): ~10 g.

Total ≈ 85 + 100 + 72 + 30 + 40 + 10 ≈ 337 g. Rounded for the heaped centre and hidden layers, about 350 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the spinach base is already counted; the broccoli and olives partly sit beneath cheese, which is included above.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Spinach, raw: 23
- Broccoli, cooked: 35
- Olives, cured: 115
- Parmesan: 430
- Avocado: 160
- Vinaigrette/oil dressing: 400 (mostly oil)

Energy: spinach 85 g x 0.23 = 20 kcal; broccoli 100 g x 0.35 = 35; olives 72 g x 1.15 = 83; Parmesan 30 g x 4.3 = 129; avocado 40 g x 1.6 = 64; dressing 10 g x 4.0 = 40. Total ≈ 371 kcal for ~337 g.
